metadata.case_name: YIP KWAN CHEUNG AND ANOTHER v. CHIM HONG WING

plaintiff.occupation_before: worked in the optometry industry for over 40 years

injuries.description: The 1st Plaintiff was cut on the forehead by broken glass, the 3 cm wound was sutured with 5 stitches at the hospital and left a scar
source: The 1st Plaintiff was cut on the forehead by broken glass, the 3 cm wound was sutured with 5 stitches at the hospital and left a scar
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

injuries.description: the 1st Plaintiff was also struck on the leg by debris and suffered bruising
source: and the 1st Plaintiff was also struck on the leg by debris and suffered bruising.
injuries.icd_description: Contusion of other or unspecified parts of lower leg

source: According to the Medical Report of Caritas Hospital dated May 3 2005, the diagnosis was post-head injury dizziness and patient was “reassured and discharged”.

Since the accident, the 1st Plaintiff developed post-traumatic stress disorder that was manifested in the form of nightmares, flashbacks, fear of road traffic, irritability, social anxiety, poor sleep, absent-mindedness and withdrawal.

injuries.description: The 1st Plaintiff had a history of palpitation and artial fibrillation of his heart since around 1999-2000
source: The 1st Plaintiff had a history of palpitation and artial fibrillation of his heart since around 1999-2000.

Dr. Kum Chi Chiu of the Prince of Wales Hospital in his medical report dated 20 May 2005 disclosed that the 1st Plaintiff suffered recurrent attacks of atrial fibrillation and was poorly controlled by medications, and eventually radio frequency ablation was carried out in August 11 2004 and by March 2005, the 1st Plaintiff’s heart condition was under control and needed no further medication.

manifestations.description: 3 cm wound sutured with 5 stitches; scar
fear of road traffic; fear of working after 11.00 p.m.; social anxiety; withdrawal
changed routine; stopped working long hours

treatments_received: treated at Caritas Hospital and discharged on the same day
3 cm forehead wound sutured with 5 stitches at the hospital
attended 9 sessions of the out patient service of the Caritas Clinical Psychology Department from 18 November 2002 to 10 June 2003
radio frequency ablation carried out on August 11 2004
treatments_future: further active psychiatric treatment for 6-12 months (estimated about 10 sessions at about $2,000 per session)

losses.description: Scar on forehead from 3 cm wound sutured with 5 stitches
social anxiety, withdrawal and change in social behaviour since the accident

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: fear of road traffic and reluctance to work late or be out late
